119.question_text: Three people complete a lap in 15 1/6 seconds, 16 1/4 seconds, and 18 2/3 seconds. After one hour, how many additional seconds pass before they are together at the starting point again?
solution_steps: The times are 91/6, 65/4, and 56/3 seconds.
Their L.C.M. is L.C.M.(91, 65, 56) ÷ H.C.F.(6, 4, 3) = 3640 seconds.
Thus they return together after 1 hour 40 seconds, so the additional time is 40 seconds.
One revolution takes 60/40, 60/24, and 60/16 seconds, or 3/2, 5/2, and 15/4 seconds.
Their L.C.M. is L.C.M.(3, 5, 15) ÷ H.C.F.(2, 2, 4) = 15/2 seconds.
Therefore, all three red spots touch the ground together again after 7 1/2 seconds.

128.question_text: The ratio of two numbers is 3:4 and their L.C.M. is 120. What is their sum?
solution_steps: Let the numbers be 3x and 4x, so their H.C.F. is x.
H.C.F. × L.C.M. = product of the numbers, so x × 120 = 3x × 4x.
Thus x = 10, the numbers are 30 and 40, and their sum is 70.
The lights therefore change together after 7 minutes 30 seconds.
Starting from 7:20:15, the next simultaneous change is at 7:27:45.
